question.text: The Vernier constant of Vernier callipers is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> and it has zero error of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>05</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>. While measuring diameter of a sphere, the main scale reading is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>7</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and coinciding vernier division is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn></math> . The corrected diameter will be _____<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Vernier constant is the least count of the vernier V.C=0.1 mm=0.01 cm

zero error =-0.05 cm

∴correction=0.05 cm

M.S.R.=1.7 cm

V.S.R.=5 V.C.=5×0.01=0.05 cm

The diameter of the sphere will be,

diameter=MSR+VSR+correction

1.7+0.05+0.05=1.8 cm

=180×10-2 cm
